[Open the Ska / reggae style in the Backing Track](../tools/backing-track.html?style=reggae){.btn .btn-outline-primary}

## What it is

Jamaican popular music since about 1960: guitar and keyboard chords on the off-beats (the *skank*), a bass
that carries the melody of the groove, and, in reggae, a **one-drop** drum beat with nothing on beat 1 and
the kick and snare (or rim) together on beat 3.

## A little history

**Ska** (c. 1960-66) came from Jamaican musicians playing American R&B for sound systems and stressing
the off-beat; studio bands such as the Skatalites played it fast with horns. Around 1966 the tempo slowed
into **rocksteady**, with the bass more prominent (Alton Ellis, the Paragons). By 1968 the beat had
changed again into **reggae**: Toots and the Maytals' *Do the Reggay* (1968) is one of the first records
to use the word. Drummer Carlton Barrett of Bob Marley's Wailers made the one-drop the standard reggae
beat, and Island Records' *Catch a Fire* (1973) took the Wailers worldwide. Later strands include dub,
roots, lovers rock, dancehall (see [Reggaeton](reggaeton.qmd)) and Britain's 2 Tone ska revival (c. 1979).

## The band's version

- **Bass:** *Roots on every beat*, plainer than a real reggae bass line, which moves and leaves gaps.
- **Comping:** off-beat chords. **Drums:** one-drop.

## Listening

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| The Skatalites, *Guns of Navarone* | 1965 | Ska: fast, horns, the off-beat guitar. |
| Alton Ellis, *Rock Steady* | 1967 | The slower rocksteady groove. |
| Desmond Dekker & the Aces, *Israelites* | 1968 | Early reggae; a UK number one in 1969. |
| Toots and the Maytals, *Do the Reggay* | 1968 | The name on a record. |
| Bob Marley & the Wailers, *Stir It Up* (*Catch a Fire*) | 1973 | Carlton Barrett's one-drop, Aston Barrett's bass. |

### More recent

| Recording | Year | Listen for |
|---|---|---|
| Sublime, *Santeria* | 1996 | Off-beat guitar and a one-drop feel in American alt-rock. |
| No Doubt, *Underneath It All* | 2001 | Recorded in Jamaica with Sly & Robbie. |
| Damian Marley, *Welcome to Jamrock* | 2005 | Modern roots reggae. |
| Rihanna, *Man Down* | 2011 | A one-drop under a pop singer. |

- David Katz, *Solid Foundation: An Oral History of Reggae* (Bloomsbury, 2003).
